summary: On 2 November 2023 a power failure at a Flexential data center in Portland took down the primary site for Cloudflare's control plane and analytics. Customers could not change settings and logs were lost for about two days.

overview.background: Cloudflare ran its control plane (dashboard and APIs) and analytics from three core data centers, with a disaster recovery site in Europe. PDX-04 held critical services including Kafka and ClickHouse.
overview.impact: The dashboard, APIs and analytics were disrupted. Network and security traffic was not affected. Some logs were permanently lost, and unreplicated datasets have gaps.
overview.severity: Control-plane outage from 11:44 UTC on 2 November to 04:25 on 4 November.
overview.gaps: Parts of the post are labelled by Cloudflare as informed speculation about Flexential.

timeline.e: An unplanned PGE maintenance event shuts one power feed to PDX-04. Flexential keeps the other utility feed and starts generators.
A ground fault on a PGE transformer shuts down the facility's generators and utility feeds.
Cloudflare's two routers at the facility go offline.
Generators restart and parts of the facility get power. Cloudflare's circuit breakers are faulty and need replacing.
Cloudflare fails over a small share of the control plane to its European DR sites.
Migrated services are stable and most customers are no longer directly affected.
Flexential restores both utility feeds and confirms clean power.
Cloudflare begins a full bootstrap of PDX-04 servers.

rootCause.trigger: A ground fault on a PGE transformer shut down both the facility's generators and utility feeds.
rootCause.underlying: UPS batteries ran out before power returned. Cloudflare's Kafka and ClickHouse services depended on the site and were not fully covered by failover, and a full facility loss had never been tested.
contributing: Flexential did not tell Cloudflare it had failed over to generators
Some newer products were not on the disaster recovery site
A thundering herd of API calls had to be rate limited on recovery

evidence.label: The provider
evidence.body: Counter to best practices, Flexential did not inform Cloudflare that they had failed over to generator power.

evidence.label: The verdict
evidence.body: To start, this never should have happened.

evidence.label: A simulated failover test
evidence.body:
$ chaos run --target dc=pdx-04 --action power-off --duration 30m
expected: dashboard p99 < 2s, no log loss
result: FAIL kafka-consumer-lag growing
evidence.note: Shows a facility-loss test. Invented output.

diagnose.step: Check facility power and network reachability.
diagnose.why: Routers at the site went offline first.

diagnose.step: Identify which services depend on the site.

correct.step: Fail over what is covered to the DR site.
correct.why: Cloudflare failed over a part of the control plane.
A thundering herd hit the APIs.

correct.step: Rebuild the rest from the site once power is stable.

verify.step: Check dashboard, API and log pipelines separately.
verify.why: Each recovered on its own timeline.

prevent.step: Remove control plane dependencies on core data centers.
Require tested DR for GA products.
Create a DR plan for logs.

fix.safety: Bootstrapping a facility after power loss can overload shared services. Rate limit and stage it.

troubleshoot.scenario: Your primary facility lost all power and your control plane is partly down. Logs are dropping.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do and in what order?
hints: How do you stop a thundering herd?
troubleshoot.answer: Fail over covered services, rate limit recovery, communicate, rebuild the site once power is stable, then test full facility loss and extend DR to all products.

remediation.answer: Every GA product must run on the HA cluster with a tested failover.
Replicate logs to a second site before processing.

design.prompt: Design a control plane that survives the loss of its main facility.
design.answer: Distribute the control plane, replicate stateful systems, test removal of each site and rate limit recovery.
